entry.label: Black box
entry.description: A black box is a system treated through observable inputs, outputs and behaviour while its internal organisation remains unknown, inaccessible or deliberately bracketed. The move is selective: what counts as input, output and relevant behaviour still depends on purpose, boundary and observer.

profile.title: Black box
profile.canonical_definition: A black box is a system treated through observable inputs, outputs and behaviour while its internal organisation remains unknown, inaccessible or deliberately bracketed. The move is selective: what counts as input, output and relevant behaviour still depends on purpose, boundary and observer.
profile.summary: An investigation chooses inputs, outputs, and conditions to record. A finite consistent record leaves untried behaviour uncertain; even matching behaviour at a chosen interface need not identify a unique internal arrangement.
profile.why_it_matters: A useful description depends on what was observed, what could be tested, and which distinctions were retained. Further tests can distinguish predictions when the relevant conditions are accessible and repeatable.
key_distinctions: matching stipulated behaviour and matching finite trials
a valid grouping and an arbitrary simplification
practice_connections: Record the sequence, conditions, inputs, and outputs
Ask which test would distinguish competing predictions
Note inaccessible states and limits of grouping
common_misreadings: A finite record determines every untested response
A matching interface uniquely identifies an internal mechanism
profile.editorial_note: Source-scoped research candidate; human editorial acceptance remains pending. Grammar of Systems' named principles are separate statements.
